newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures recovered from session lows after U.S. bonds reacted favourably to a larger than expected decline in a U.S. January purchasing managers survey, while PIBOR contracts continued to come pressure.
Traders in Paris said some U.S. funds were steady sellers of both PIBOR contracts and the French franc throughout the day.
They said the franc was suffering along with other European currencies, notably the Italian lira and peseta, after a wave of mark buying.
The franc fell as low as 3.3797 against the German unit from 3.3764 on Friday, its lowest level since January 9.
However, one trader said there was little concern with the franc. "There's no need to worry about the franc, even if it reaches 3.38," he said.

Damien Jamet, analyst at FIMAT, said that he thought PIBOR contracts and the short end of the yield curve were continuing to suffer from recent statements by Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet and Bundesbank members dampening, if not killing, hopes for more, speedy, cuts in key short-term rates.
March PIBOR fell four basis points to 96.63, dropping through support at 96.46/65 just prior to the close. June fared even worse, declining five basis points.
However, Jamet said the short end should stabilise soon, as European rates would remain low for a long time to come.
Bond analysts said the focus in France would remain on the United States with a key Federal Reserve monetary policy meeting starting on Tuesday and jobs data due on Friday.

They said few expected any increase in U.S. rates at this meeting and the bond market would be unlikely to move much higher, as such an outcome was already discounted and the risk was that rates would have to go up at some stage.
The spread between French and German 10-year bond yields narrowed slightly to minus 15 basis points from minus 16.
